data.narrative:
Alif Semiconductor is a Series C-stage chip design company that has raised $185.9M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 3 public semiconductor firms (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers, with particular weight on 3 same-stage private comps: Etched ($5.0B), d-Matrix ($2.0B), and DEEPX ($529M).

Two quantitative methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $186M total raised proxy, yielding $316M. Peer-median anchoring across the 3 same-sector, same-stage private comparables produces a $2.0B implied value, with a peer range of $529M to $5.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (median 21.5x across the sector) cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure. The wide private peer dispersion ($529M–$5.0B) reflects material heterogeneity in chip-company trajectories and business model maturity.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $269M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.2B. This 8.5x spread reflects uncertainty around the target's technical differentiation, commercial traction, and capital intensity relative to peers. Key uncertainties include revenue run-rate, gross margins, and the addressability of its target silicon application—factors that explain why Etched trades at 9.5x the valuation of DEEPX despite identical staging.
